title: A user cannot reach a private application at all
aliases: zpa no log record for user

prose.text: The first question is whether the request ever entered ZPA, and the second is what the record says.

prose.label: Before ZPA.
prose.text: {{zcc-intercepts-defined-apps}} {{other-traffic-elsewhere}} {{unmatched-not-forwarded}} The client state is not sourced {{gap:zcc-active-state}}.

prose.label: Segment match.
prose.text: Which segment wins, port misses and carve-outs are in [[zpa.app-segments.matching]], and Bypass in [[zpa.app-segments.bypass]]. A port miss is described both as a bypass and as a drop [[zpa.app-segments.matching]].

prose.label: No record.
prose.text: A request dropped at the client is [[zpa.policy.multimatch]]; that the absence of a record always means this is not sourced {{gap:no-record-means-client-side}}.

prose.label: A record that closed.
prose.text: The fields are in [[zpa.troubleshooting.log-fields]]; reading Close together with the Policy field is not sourced {{gap:reading-close-and-policy}}.

prose.label: Policy.
prose.text: Order, first match and the default are in [[zpa.policy.evaluation-order]]. A forwarding bypass that leaves no record, and an empty Policy field on a blocked session, are not sourced {{gap:bypass-leaves-no-record}}.

checks.do: Whether the destination host and port are covered by an application segment at all, since traffic outside any segment is not forwarded to Private Access.
Which segment is the most granular match and whether the destination port is in it, or whether the request was bypassed or dropped at the client.
Whether a more specific segment for the host carved it out of the wildcard segment, and whether the missing port or Multimatch fixes it.
Whether any segment for the same FQDN has Bypass set to Always, which then takes precedence.
Whether a client forwarding rule bypasses the traffic before access policy is evaluated.
Whether a User Activity record exists, then its Policy, ConnectionStatus and Connector fields, noting that the absence of a record is not shown to mean a client-side drop.
Which access rule matched first, and that no matching rule means the request is blocked.
Whether the connector ID is zero or empty and which session status code accompanies it.

zcc-intercepts-defined-apps.statement: Zscaler Client Connector recognizes the internal applications that are available via Private Access (access to them is defined in Private Access policies), intercepts the user requests for them and forwards those requests to the Zero Trust Exchange.

quotes: it intercepts the user requests for those applications, and then forwards those requests to the ZTE.
Zscaler Client Connector recognizes the internal applications that are available via Private Access.
Access to these applications is defined in Private Access based on policies.

other-traffic-elsewhere.statement: Zscaler Client Connector forwards traffic for internal applications to Private Access and other traffic goes to Internet & SaaS.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector identifies internal applications to forward traffic to Private Access, and other traffic goes to Internet & SaaS.

unmatched-not-forwarded.statement: A destination that no application segment covers is not forwarded to Private Access.
unmatched-not-forwarded.conditions: Inference: the client intercepts requests for applications defined in Private Access and sends other traffic elsewhere, so a destination outside every segment is not an application defined in Private Access. The sources do not use the phrase 'not in any segment'.

zcc-active-state.title: Client enrollment and tunnel state
zcc-active-state.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Confirm ZCC is enrolled and the Z-Tunnel is established. ZCC must show the Private Access state as active, not disconnected or in bypass." No captured source describes a Private Access state indicator in the client.

no-record-means-client-side.title: No log record means a client-side drop
no-record-means-client-side.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "If there is no LSS record, the request never reached the ZPA Service Edge. If no LSS record exists at all, the request was dropped client-side before reaching the ZPA Service Edge." The policy-multimatch subject sources that a request dropped at the client is not sent to Private Access; no source says the converse, that every missing record is a client-side drop (a stream gap or a receiver filter would also leave none).

reading-close-and-policy.title: Reading a Close record with a Policy value or an empty one
reading-close-and-policy.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "A `Close` or absent record combined with a policy block name is the typical signal. A named block rule in `Policy` -> access policy denied the request. Empty `Policy` field or a reason pointing to connector or server -> the policy allowed but the path from the App Connector to the application server failed. The LSS User Activity log shows `ConnectionStatus = Close` with an `InternalReason` indicating a connector-to-server setup failure, and `ConnectionSetupTime` will be disproportionately high." The Policy field is the access policy rule name (policy-field) and the Close value is not defined (status-meanings); neither reading is stated by a source.

bypass-leaves-no-record.title: Bypass leaves no record; an empty Policy field on a blocked session
bypass-leaves-no-record.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "If any segment covering the FQDN has `bypass_type = Always`, ZCC sends traffic directly and ZPA records nothing. If `Policy` is empty and the session was blocked, one of two things happened: (a) the forwarding policy bypassed ZPA before access policy evaluated, or (b) the segment was not in any policy rule's scope." That a forwarding or segment bypass sends traffic direct is sourced in the policy and segment subjects; that ZPA records nothing for it, and that these are the only two explanations of a blocked session with an empty Policy field, are not.
